title: The Planet Where It Rains Diamonds
hook: Guess what falls from the sky on Neptune — whatever you pictured is wrong.
script: Guess what falls from the sky on Neptune — whatever you pictured is wrong. What if you could actually stand beneath that deep blue storm? Ten thousand kilometers down, atmospheric pressure violently strips carbon out of methane gas. Pressure like fifteen hundred elephants on a postage stamp squeezes that carbon into diamond rain. They sink like slow boulders. Near the core, they pool into an ocean where solid diamond icebergs drift. In the outer solar system, our rarest treasure is just regular weather.

captions: Could you imagine diamond rain falling like hail? Which planet has the wildest weather?
Deep inside Neptune and Uranus, carbon gets squeezed into literal gemstones.
The strangest weather in our solar system doesn't make water — it makes diamonds.
